classification.difficultyReason: Select a minimum spanning tree from a seven-house weighted network and sum its six cable lengths.

content.prompt: What is the minimum amount of cable needed to connect these houses? (All units are in metres.)

spec.description: Seven recognisable house markers retain their relative positions and all twelve weighted connections. Position identifiers are internal and are not printed. Ordinary edges and house outlines use house-style black.
spec.mathematics: Undirected network: upper-left–top 15; upper-left–interior 8.8; interior–top 9.2; top–right-middle 10.4; top–bottom-central 22; upper-left–lower-left 10; upper-left–bottom-central 14.5; interior–bottom-central 11; lower-left–bottom-central 9; bottom-central–right-middle 15.6; bottom-central–lower-right 8.5; right-middle–lower-right 8.
spec.answerVisibility: All weights and houses are permanent givens; no selected spanning-tree edges or answer appear in the student diagram.

answer.worked:
Choose the edges of lengths $8$, $8.5$, $8.8$, $9$ and $9.2$ metres, then the $10$ metre edge joining the upper-left and lower-left houses. These six edges connect all seven houses without a cycle, forming a minimum spanning tree.
$$8+8.5+8.8+9+9.2+10=53.5$$
The minimum cable length is $53.5\text{ m}$.
